rockTypePanel.basaltSummary: Fine-grained volcanic rock, often forming columns, faces, and solid cracks.
rockTypePanel.basaltTips: Usually sounder when wet than sandstone, but check local loose blocks.
rockTypePanel.blurbWithPct: I climb mostly on {name} ({percent}% of tagged ascents).
rockTypePanel.chossSummary: Loose, poorly cemented rock — adventure climbing more than textbook geology.
rockTypePanel.chossTips: Helmets, careful testing of holds, and ground-up caution are the game.
rockTypePanel.conglomerateSummary: Pebbles cemented in a matrix — climbing on glued-in cobbles and weird features.
rockTypePanel.conglomerateTips: Trust holds carefully; matrix quality varies wildly between crags.
rockTypePanel.dolomiteSummary: Carbonate rock related to limestone, often forming steep alpine walls and towers.
rockTypePanel.dolomiteTips: Can be polished or friable depending on the formation — treat like limestone for wet conditions.
rockTypePanel.fallbackSummary: Tagged as {name} on theCrag — rock character varies by area.
rockTypePanel.fallbackTips: Check local topos and ethics; conditions (especially wet rock) matter for softer rock types.
rockTypePanel.gneissSummary: Banded metamorphic rock with mixed crystal textures and solid alpine faces.
rockTypePanel.gneissTips: Quality varies by banding; often similar feel to granite with more variety in holds.
rockTypePanel.graniteSummary: Hard igneous rock with quartz and feldspar — famous for friction slabs, crystals, and splitter cracks (think Yosemite-style).
rockTypePanel.graniteTips: Often condition-dependent: grippy when cool, slicker when hot. Sharp crystals can be hard on skin.
rockTypePanel.gritstoneSummary: Coarse, hard sandstone (UK Peak District classic) with outstanding friction on rounded breaks and arêtes.
rockTypePanel.gritstoneTips: Trad ethic is strong; fragile when wet — stay off after rain.
rockTypePanel.limestoneSummary: Calcium-carbonate rock that forms pockets, tufas, caves, and steep sport walls common in Europe.
rockTypePanel.limestoneTips: Popular routes polish easily. Cracks are less common than on granite, so many crags are bolted.
rockTypePanel.quartziteSummary: Metamorphosed sandstone — very hard, often sharp and friction-rich.
rockTypePanel.quartziteTips: Can be abrasive on skin and shoes; holds tend to be positive when featured.
rockTypePanel.sandstoneSummary: Sedimentary rock of cemented sand grains — rough friction, pockets, and dramatic desert features.
rockTypePanel.sandstoneTips: Avoid climbing when wet: soft sandstone can break holds. Let it dry thoroughly after rain.
rockTypePanel.slateSummary: Fine metamorphic rock with smooth, often technical faces and small edges.
rockTypePanel.slateTips: Friction can feel glassy; careful footwork matters more than raw strength.
rockTypePanel.volcanicSummary: Basalt and related volcanics — often solid with positive edges, columns, or blocky features.
rockTypePanel.volcanicTips: Quality varies by flow; some areas are bombproof, others loose on the edges.

logbook.hint: From/to dates are inclusive. Unknown style finds missing, blank, or literal Unknown route styles, even with an ascent protection override; Other finds present, unsupported route styles. Route grade min/max use your display system and exclude boulders (filter style for those). Missing route data finds routes without a recorded height, bolt count, or cached pitch list after route info was fetched. No pitch list cached also matches single-pitch and boulder routes when theCrag omits pitches, so it is not a list of multipitch routes missing data. The pitch-list filter excludes routes whose route info was never fetched (History not checked is a separate, route-history filter); Tag contains searches tag names; Exact tag matches Category:Name (case-insensitive, repeat `tagExact` in the URL for AND). Categories include Rock type, Steepness, Aspect, Style, Weather, Walk in time, Legality, and Condition when shown on chips. Project filters exclude unknown flags. No setter credit found includes routes whose history has not been imported. Weather filters use the opt-in Open-Meteo cache and only match outdoor ascents with cached weather for that day; the owner can also list outdoor ascents with no weather cached yet.

projectDetail.leadReadinessRecalculated: Readiness is recalculated using evidence available by each climbing day. Logged effort measures practice, not moves completed.
projectDetail.leadSupportingPyramid: Supporting pyramid in the past 365 days, in this discipline and grade scale: {n1}/2 distinct routes one grade step below; {n2}/4 two steps below.
projectDetail.methodPoints: Up to 15 points come from unsuccessful tries on this project, against a soft target of 15 (short-term), 35 (medium) or 75 (long-haul). The horizon follows the gap to your best recent send: at most one step, two steps, or more. The base model caps at 94%. The first session establishes the baseline; each additional valid climbing day on this route adds one readiness point, up to 99%. Only a logged send reaches 100%. An unknown grade has no readiness estimate.
projectDetail.methodRanges: Remaining-work ranges are the middle half of your comparable completed projects, after subtracting your logged work. At least three longer projects are required for each range; estimates disappear when there is too little evidence or you have exceeded that history. These are personal historical comparisons, with no claim of scientific validation.
projectDetail.methodReadiness: Readiness uses the past 365 days of outdoor sends on distinct routes in the same discipline and grade scale. A best send at this grade or above contributes 60 points, one step below 35, or two steps below 10. Up to 20 points come from two routes one step below, and 25 from four routes two steps below.
projectDetail.methodSessions: One session is one valid written calendar day. Failed tries use the logged attempt count, or one when missing. A send count includes its successful try; its implied failures and separate failure entries use the larger total to avoid double counting. Invalid and future dates do not contribute to estimates. Private comments are never used.
projectDetail.noteProjectSent: This project is sent. The session history below records the work and later repeats.
projectDetail.noteRoughComparison: This is a rough comparison with completed projects, not a prediction. Unsent projects and unlogged tries are absent; a send can come earlier or much later.
projectDetail.summary: How approximate readiness and estimates work
projectDetail.summaryTotals: {sessions, plural, one {# session} other {# sessions}} · {tries, plural, one {# unsuccessful try} other {# unsuccessful tries}} · {sends, plural, one {# send} other {# sends}}

projects.leadIncludeDismiss: Include or dismiss routes with Project selection here or in the {logbook}.

seasonality.coverage: Search covers only climbs in your synced logbook. {covered} of {total} matching climbs have cached monthly data. Missing data stays unknown.
seasonality.coverageHint: Seasonality is cached by the optional route-history import after sync.
seasonality.explanation: {count} {noun} with monthly data · {month}. Selected-month sorting compares the month’s percentage of each annual peak, highest first; names break ties. No “in season” cutoff is applied. Crag curves are weighted by your ascents on routes with data.
seasonality.intro: Explore theCrag’s community climbing patterns by month. These are seasonal patterns, not a weather forecast or conditions on your visits.
seasonality.noLoggedClimbsMatch: No logged climbs match this search.

seasonality.pageDescription: Search your cached crags and climbs by month using theCrag seasonality.
seasonality.tryAnotherName: Try another name or clear your search.

settings.bannerCsvDoesNotRemove: Manual CSV uploads do not remove missing entries.
settings.bannerImportsRunSeparately: Route data and weather imports run separately when enabled.
settings.bannerRouteDataReady: Route data is ready to check again.
settings.bannerRouteDataWaiting: Route data can be checked again in {when}.
settings.bannerWeatherReady: Weather import is ready to run again.
settings.bannerWeatherWaiting: Weather import can run again in {when}.
settings.dateFormatAutoHint: Derives format from the configured display locale
settings.dateFormatDmyHint: UK, Australia, Europe, and Latin America
settings.hintApiKeyIntro: Uses {key} from your environment. Keys grant read access to private notes — treat them like passwords. {docs}
settings.hintBoulderGrades: Boulders and V-graded highballs. Both choices apply for every visitor.
settings.hintCountedTickTypes: Configure which tick types count in dashboard and page totals, projects, and goals. The logbook always lists every logged ascent.
settings.hintCsvImport: For everyone without supporter API access. Export from theCrag: {action}, then upload the file here whenever you want to refresh. CSV import upserts rows but does **not** remove missing entries. API sync reconciles deletions. {syncOptions}
settings.hintDateFormat: Controls date layout across the logbook, heatmaps, and charts.
settings.hintDatesAreDisplayOnly: Dates and measurements are display-only: stored data, badge thresholds, and filters stay metric.
settings.hintEndYourSignedInSession: End your signed-in session on this device. You will need the app password to return.
settings.hintIntro: Sync, display preferences, search visibility, imports and local data control.
settings.hintLanguage: Default interface language. Set to Auto to match each visitor's browser language. Visitors can also change their preferred language via the header.
settings.hintNoApiKey: No API key configured. Set {key} in {env}, or use **CSV import** above to upload your logbook export by hand.
settings.hintCsvOnlyRouteData: This install keeps its logbook in CSV: no API sync runs, so uploaded ascents are never pruned. {key} is still used for route data and area lookups.
settings.hintRouteDataNeedsOwnerLogin: CSV imports don't carry your {login}, so set {ownerLogin} to match your FA / FFA credits.
settings.hintNotes: Shows the notes from your theCrag ticks in the logbook, and lets logbook search match them.
settings.hintNotesNoPassword: **No {appPassword} is set, so anyone who can open this site will see them.**
settings.hintNotesNoPasswordTail: Best for offline or home-network installs.
settings.hintNotesSignedIn: Only shown while you're logged in. Visitors never see them.
settings.hintPrivacy: Revoking a theCrag key does not delete data already synced here. Wipe only removes the **local** SQLite copy on this machine — it never deletes your theCrag logbook. See {privacy}.
settings.hintReAppliesMarksFromHistory: Re-applies marks from history already saved here. No requests to theCrag.
settings.hintReapplyUnmarked: Off by default: routes you unmarked stay unmarked.
settings.hintRefreshAllRoutes: Check every route again, still {count} per run. Only useful if theCrag's history was corrected. After re-fetching, use {reapply} (tick **Replace existing** if you want corrected history to overwrite current marks).
settings.hintReplaceExistingMarks: Off by default: marks you set stay as they are.
settings.hintRouteDataDisabled: Off. To turn it on, set {import} in {env} and restart. theCrag blocks plain server requests to its route API, so this uses browser impersonation ({impers}). It's at your own risk under theCrag's terms; manual FA marks always work. Renamed from {oldImport}, which no longer has any effect.
settings.hintRouteDataFetchOnce: Each route is checked once unless you request a refresh.
settings.hintRouteDataIntro: Caches route details for routes in your logbook from theCrag (popularity, ascent counts, quality, seasonality, beta, location, pitches, and flags) along with their public history. FA / FFA entries that name your {login} are marked as yours.
settings.hintRouteDataRefresh: Reload this page to update route data availability.
settings.hintRouteDataRefreshCycle: Route data is queued for refresh after {days} days.
settings.hintRouteDataTail: Up to {count} routes per run, at most one request a second, after each logbook sync and on the background import schedule. When weather import is on, remaining requests also check crag/sector locations, including for CSV imports. {docs}
settings.hintRouteGrades: Sport, trad, top rope, and other roped climbing.
settings.hintSearchIndexing: Untick to ask Google & co. not to index this site ({robots}, {noindex} meta tag, and {xRobotsTag} header). Settings and login are never indexed.
settings.hintSearchIndexingForcedOff: Off — the whole site is password protected ({authScope}).
settings.hintTemperature: Daily highs, lows, and weather conditions.
settings.hintTickLeftovers: Saved for tick types with no logged ascents — these stay live for future climbs but are not listed above: {leftover}. Choose {allTicks} and save to clear them.
settings.hintUpstreamSourceOfTruth: **Upstream is source of truth.** Each sync pulls the full logbook, updates changed ascents (comments, grades, ticks), and deletes local rows that were removed on theCrag.
settings.hintWeatherDisabled: Off. To turn it on, set {import} in {env} and restart. Uses Open-Meteo's free non-commercial archive API — fine for personal self-hosted installs.
settings.hintWeatherIntro: Caches daily outdoor weather (Open-Meteo) for logbook days that have a usable route/crag weather location. Powers heat, freeze, rain, snow, and wind badges. Up to {count} days per run, at most one request a second, after each logbook sync. {docs}
settings.hintWeatherNoDays: No weather days ready to fetch. Weather needs a usable route/crag location and a valid past climbing date.
settings.hintWeatherUnresolved: Check pending route data and weather locations above, then {review}. CSV imports can use the configured supporter key for crag/sector lookups when route data import is enabled.
settings.hintWindSpeed: Windy and calm day weather filters.
settings.linkReviewWeatherLocations: Review weather locations and choose a nearby place for missing locations

share.lead: Live cards for a blog, forum signature or profile page. They're plain images, so they work anywhere that accepts an `` or Markdown, and they update after each sync. Cards only show totals, grades and route names, never ascent notes or partners.
share.warnPrivateHost: **Only you can see these right now.** This site is at {origin}, a local or private-network address, so the links and images below won't load for anyone else. To share them, host Crag Stats on a public server or domain (a VPS, or a tunnel such as Cloudflare Tunnel), then open this page from that address and copy the code again.

trainingLoad.lead: How hard you've been climbing lately versus what you're used to — the acute:chronic workload ratio used in sports science and climbing coaching. Treat the bands as a nudge, not a diagnosis.
trainingLoad.pageDescription: Acute:chronic training load, weekly and daily intensity from your climbing logbook.

weather.hintCoverageTotals: Unresolved ascents are excluded from the location-day totals. Unavailable days have already been checked and are not automatically queued again. Viewing this page never starts an import.
weather.hintLocationQuality: Weather may use route, crag or sector points, an approximate area polygon, or an owner-selected nearby place. Terrain, elevation and distance can change conditions at the cliff. Nearby-place and polygon weather is included in these views but does not unlock weather badges. The logbook shows each ascent's location source.
weather.labelNotCheckedYet: Not checked yet (including today or future dates)
weather.labelOutdoorAscentsWithoutLocation: Outdoor ascents with a valid day but no resolved location
weather.labelResolvedLocationDays: Outdoor location-days with a resolved location
weather.lead: Historical weather on the days you climbed outdoors. These are modelled daily conditions at cached locations, not measurements at the wall or a forecast.
weather.leadCoverage: A location-day is one calendar day at one weather location, rounded to 0.1°. Visiting two locations in a day can count twice. Conditions include all outdoor ticks; performance includes only sends and attempts, so their totals can differ. Logbook links list ascents rather than location-days.
weather.leadNoPerformanceData: There are no outdoor sends or attempts with cached weather to compare yet.
weather.leadNoWeatherCached: Weather appears after the owner enables weather import and eligible outdoor location-days have been fetched. Indoor climbs are excluded. {weatherImport}.
weather.pageDescription: Historical weather on your outdoor climbing days and patterns in your logged sends and attempts.
weather.titleNoWeatherCachedForOutdoor: No weather cached for outdoor climbs yet

weatherLocations.buttonUsePlace: Use {name} as an approximate weather place
weatherLocations.emptyNoMatchingPlaces: No matching places. Try a nearby town with its region.
weatherLocations.labelChosenFallback: Chosen fallback: {name}. Precise route/crag points still take priority.
weatherLocations.leadLocationPriority: Route points take priority, then crag points, then immediate sector points. Validated small area polygons supply an approximate boundary coordinate when these points are missing. Country centres are excluded when the original payload identifies them. Without a usable point, choose a nearby town as an approximate weather location. Polygon and town fallbacks do not move route maps or unlock weather badges. Existing weather stays cached, but only the current location's key is used.
weatherLocations.leadSearchPrivacy: Search sends only the place name and country code you enter to Open-Meteo/GeoNames when you submit. No ascent details or private notes are sent. Results are cached for 30 days; no place is selected automatically.
